# 📜 OCR / HTR with Gemini

Read text off **scanned PDFs** and **photographs** — printed books and newspapers (OCR)
as well as handwritten letters and manuscripts (HTR), in any language.

**Run the steps in order, from top to bottom.** Each one has a ▶️ button on its left.

> ⚠️ **Before uploading research material, read Step 1's privacy notice.** These
> institutional notebooks require a billing-enabled project and any ethics/DPO approval
> applicable to the material. Regional Gemini API terms differ.

## Step 1: Prepare the notebook ⚙️

Click the ▶ button beside the code below. If Google asks whether to run this notebook,
check that you opened the ZMO repository, then continue. Wait for **Setup complete**
before moving on. You do not need to change the code or select a GPU.

Run each numbered cell in order. Some cells display a form: fill it in and click its
button before continuing. If you see a red error, stop at that step and read the message.
After a disconnected session, start again from Step 1.

## Step 2: Connect your Gemini API key 🔑

An API key lets this notebook use your Google AI project. Create one at
[Google AI Studio](https://aistudio.google.com/apikey). Creating a key and paying for
processing are separate: use the billing-enabled project required by Step 1.

Run the cell below and follow **Colab Secrets** instructions. Enable **Notebook access**
for each notebook separately. Never paste a key into the code or share it with anyone.

# ============================================
# STEP 2 — API KEY (Colab Secrets first)
# ============================================
key_panel = zc.ApiKeyPanel()
key_panel.display()
display(HTML(zc.api_key_migration_notice()))

## Step 2.5: Connect Google Drive (strongly recommended) ☁️

With Drive connected, local page checkpoints are copied in small batches with retries and
verified at the end. Always download the final ZIP if Drive verification reports a failure.

You can also load large PDFs directly from Drive.

## Step 3: Choose your documents 📁

**Supported:** PDF, JPG, PNG, WEBP, HEIC

For best results scan at 300 DPI or more. Images use high detail; PDF pages use medium detail. Check a few pages first.

# ============================================
# STEP 3 — CHOOSE FILES
# ============================================
file_selector = zc.FileSelector(
    dest_dir=FOLDERS['input'],
    extensions=ALL_EXTENSIONS,
    drive=drive,
    icon_for=document_icon,
    what='documents',
)
file_selector.display()

## Step 4: Settings 🎛️

Choose a fixed model release and decide which scholarly representation you need:

- **Diplomatic transcription** preserves lineation, punctuation, and hyphenation.
- **Normalized reading text** joins wrapped lines and removes only clear line-break hyphens.

For defensible results, test a few pages against manually checked ground truth before a long run.

## Step 5: Preview and run / resume

Preview scope before sending data. Resume with the same source and settings to reuse completed rows, pages, or segments. Changed settings start a separate run. Batch jobs must be collected or cancelled before switching that run to synchronous processing.

## Step 6: Download, recover, and review

Download a recovery ZIP, including partial output, provenance, and resume state. Import it after a runtime reset. Re-select the original source to resume. The review panel keeps corrections separate from the original model output.

## Optional: temporary files

Temporary audio segments and upload buffers are cleaned automatically. Keep run folders and recovery ZIPs while work is active. Colab removes local files when the runtime ends.
print("Keep your recovery ZIPs and Drive run folders until you have verified your results.")

## Help

- A run is identified by source bytes, model, prompts, and settings. Matching runs resume automatically.
- Each completed unit is saved locally. Drive synchronization happens at export checkpoints; download the recovery ZIP if a mirror fails.
- A partial, failed, or truncated unit remains eligible for retry. Keep the raw output for comparison.
- Excel formulas need cached values: recalculate and save the source in Excel or LibreOffice when preflight flags a missing cache. Generated cells are always literal text.
- PDF text-layer extraction is an explicit option. Inspect the samples first; the existing layer may itself contain OCR errors.
- Request and price estimates exclude retries, thinking, and provider-specific media tokenization. They are planning estimates, not billing caps.
- For CLI, recovery details, and evaluation, see [the project documentation](https://github.com/fmadore/zmo-ai-pipelines).
